business_problem: JCB needed to modernize long-running on-premises business systems so it could improve agility, reduce infrastructure and operating costs, shorten API delivery times, and create a shared data platform for new financial-services initiatives.
solution_summary: JCB is building common infrastructure and data infrastructure on AWS as part of a long-running migration of business systems from on premises. Transaction and operational systems are being standardized across Amazon Aurora and Amazon DynamoDB, secured with AWS WAF and AWS PrivateLink, and connected through a growing API layer. In parallel, data from those systems is consolidated in Amazon S3, cataloged with AWS Glue, and queried with Amazon Athena to create a shared data platform that supports business initiatives and faster service integration. Using AWS Cloud Adoption Framework guidance and PCI DSS-aligned controls, JCB has been able to reduce infrastructure lead times, expand the number of linked systems, and create a more agile foundation for financial-services innovation at scale.

solution_components.name: Amazon Aurora
solution_components.role: Supports standardized relational workloads in JCB's common AWS infrastructure.

solution_components.name: Amazon DynamoDB
solution_components.role: Handles scalable NoSQL application data in migrated business systems.

solution_components.name: AWS WAF
solution_components.role: Protects customer-facing and API-facing traffic in the new platform.

solution_components.name: Amazon S3
solution_components.role: Stores data for JCB's shared data infrastructure.

solution_components.name: AWS Glue
solution_components.role: Catalogs and prepares data inside the common data platform.

solution_components.name: Amazon Athena
solution_components.role: Queries data in the shared platform for analytics and business use.

solution_components.name: AWS PrivateLink
solution_components.role: Provides private connectivity between services in the migrated environment.

data_flow: Business-system data from migrated applications is stored on the common AWS platform, consolidated in Amazon S3, prepared with AWS Glue, queried with Amazon Athena, and exposed to linked systems and APIs while operational traffic is protected by AWS WAF and private connectivity patterns.
business_outcome: JCB expects to cut infrastructure costs by about 30 percent, reduced API infrastructure delivery from 6 months to 3 months, grew linked APIs to more than 100, and had 54 systems running on AWS as of March 2023 on the way to migrating 80 systems and expanding data from 32 TB toward 120 TB.
